findings.claim: The race entry moves the touch slots with a transform. zones() measures them with getBoundingClientRect and caches the result until enter(false) at GO. A touch during the roughly 560 ms slide caches the shifted rects, so for the rest of the countdown presses on GAS, BRAKE or the steer pads miss. A thumb held on GAS through GO also gives no throttle.
findings.evidence: `enter(on) { element.classList.toggle('is-entering', on); invalidate(); }` with `zones: () => (cache ??= measure())`, and `measure()` uses `slots[id].getBoundingClientRect()`, which includes the transform. The cache is only cleared on resize, wake() or enter(). Trace at 844×390: reset() calls enter(true) and the slots get `animation: ui-touch-enter 200ms … backwards` with delays of 200–320 ms, so with backwards fill they sit at translateY(50vh) = +195 px. A pointerdown 100 ms after reset runs touch.ts:75 `hitTest(opts.zones(), …)`. That caches GAS at cy ≈ 390−21−50+195 = 514, off screen. Every later pointerdown on the real GAS position (cy ≈ 319) misses until GO runs enter(false). The finger already held there is not re-tested, because onMove only re-tests pointers that are already held. Nothing is pressed and nothing turns mustard during the countdown, and there is no throttle at GO.
findings.suggestedFix: Clear the cache when the slide ends as well as when it starts. In createTouchControls, add `element.addEventListener('animationend', invalidate)`, or check `e.target` is a slot. Another option is to skip caching while the layer has `is-entering`: `zones: () => element.classList.contains('is-entering') ? measure() : (cache ??= measure())`.

findings.claim: Restarting from the pause screen during the countdown doesn't replay the race entry. `entering` is still true because GO never came, so the reset() for the new race does nothing to the entry. The spec says a race reset slides the HUD panels and touch slots in.
findings.evidence: In race-ui.ts, `function enter(on) { if (on === entering) return; … }` and reset() calls `enter(true)`. The entry is only turned off by `if (step === 0) { enter(false); … }`. Steps: start a race, which calls reset() and sets entering = true. Pause during the countdown and press Restart, which calls game.startRace and then ui.reset(). The race layer stays visible (game.ts:156). In reset(), enter(true) returns early and hud.enter and touch.enter are guarded the same way. `is-entering` never leaves the element, so the panels sit still while the new race counts down. Restarting after GO does play the entry, because entering was false.
findings.suggestedFix: In reset(), restart the entry when it is already on. For example, call `enter(false)` and then `enter(true)` with a forced reflow in between: in hud.enter and touch.enter, read `void element.offsetWidth` after removing the class. Another option is to toggle an alternate keyframes name, like the `is-again` pattern used for the event motion.

findings.claim: The POS bump applies the stamp easing to both halves of its keyframes. The panel overshoots on the way up and again on the way down, dipping below its rest size. UI_RULES §7 and board 05 allow one overshoot at most and use the stamp easing for landings only.
findings.evidence: The rule is `.ui-hud-pos.is-bump { animation: ui-hud-bump var(--duration-stamp) var(--ease-stamp); }` and the keyframes are `@keyframes ui-hud-bump { 50% { transform: scale(var(--ui-hud-bump)); } }`. The timing function runs once per keyframe interval. cubic-bezier(.3,1.5,.5,1) peaks at y ≈ 1.08 (s ≈ 0.6: 0.432+0.432+0.216). From 0 to 50% the scale goes 1→1.12 and overshoots to about 1.13. From 50% to 100% it goes 1.12→1 and overshoots to 1 − 0.12×0.08 ≈ 0.99, below rest. That is two overshoots, and the second dips below the panel's rest size. UI_RULES §7 says stamp is 'one overshoot, landings only', and board 05 says 'one overshoot at most'.
findings.suggestedFix: Set the easing for each segment. Use snap on the way up and stamp only for the landing: `@keyframes ui-hud-bump { from { animation-timing-function: var(--ease-snap); } 50% { transform: scale(var(--ui-hud-bump)); animation-timing-function: var(--ease-stamp); } }`, and do the same in ui-hud-bump-again. The computed animation-timing-function on the element stays the stamp curve, so AC1 still holds.

checked.how: Read every new rule. Colours, durations, easings and shadows come only from tokens (--duration-*, --ease-*, --shadow-overlay); the generated tokens.css confirms the values (stamp 160, release 120, slide 200, stagger 40, the snap and stamp curves). There are no hex, rgb or font literals and no opacity, filter or gradient. Only transform and box-shadow are animated.
All of the new animations sit inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference). The press sink (.ui-tc.is-pressed transform) is outside any media query, so it stays.
The keyframes go from --shadow-overlay (6px) to the panel's own .ui-panel box-shadow: var(--shadow-hud) (3px, components.css:75). This matches the board.

checked.target: Screenshots hud-motion--steady/overtake/new-lap/entry at 844×390 vs mockup S1-S2-race-hud-touch.png
checked.how: Opened them side by side. The layout, the POS '2/4' with the mustard digit at hud-xl, LAP, map, TIME/BEST and PAUSE all match the mockup, and the clipped roll box doesn't crop the digit. The motion itself can't be judged from the stills.
The top panels use translateY(-50vh) (down from above) and the slots translateY(50vh) (up from below). The delays are stagger×0..8 in the order POS, LAP, map, timer, PAUSE, left, right, brake, gas.

Grepped hidden and display:none in src/ui and game.ts. The pause screen doesn't hide the HUD, so a resume after GO doesn't restart the animations. A restart during the countdown does skip the entry (F2).
